options_from.why: First setup copies Avery's settings and keys from the Cobblemon pack

mods.name: Alaska Fire Towers (our own mod)
mods.pinned_reason: Our own mod (source: minecraftAlaska/fire-tower, not on Modrinth): fire lookout towers, and new worlds start in one. Update by re-running tools/gen_tower.py and gradlew build there, uploading a new GitHub release, and editing this entry by hand.

mods.name: Moonlight Lib
mods.pinned_reason: Paired with the pinned Supplementaries 3.6.7 (Moonlight from the same month, May 2026); unpin together with Supplementaries.

mods.name: Supplementaries
mods.pinned_reason: Supplementaries 3.9+ (Jun 2026 on) declares breaks sodium<0.8.12, but Iris 1.8.8 for 1.21.1 needs Sodium 0.6.x; 3.6.7 is the last release before that rule. Unpin when a stable Iris for 1.21.1 supports Sodium 0.8.

mods.name: REI Craftable Fix (our own)
mods.pinned_reason: Our own client mod (source: minecraftServer/rei-craftable-fix on the host PC). Stops REI 16's craftable-only list from rebuilding every 5 ticks (tooltip flicker) when only an item's component hash changed. Update by rebuilding, uploading a new GitHub release, and editing this entry by hand.

keybinds.why: Backtick is Zoomify's zoom in this profile; semicolon is free
[ is Weaver's Paradise's upper-wear menu; apostrophe is free
I is Cobblemon's Pokemon summary; backslash is free
R is Cobblemon's 'throw Pokémon'; Iris's reload-shaders on R froze the game on every throw
O is Cobblemon's 'hide party'; the shader menu is still in Options > Video Settings > Shader Packs
B is Xaero's 'new waypoint'; G is free in this profile
Z is Xaero's 'enlarge minimap'; H is free in this profile
R is Cobblemon's throw Pokémon and Iris's reload; N is free in both profiles
F6 is First-person Model's toggle; Zoomify's secondary (cinematic) zoom is left unbound
C is the vehicle button (ship sail, plane boost, bike bell), so zoom moves to backtick, the key the host already uses
H swaps the backpack's tools; the Accessories screen (hats, trinkets) has its own button in the inventory
K toggles shaders; Show Me Your Skin's settings are under Mods on the pause menu
J is Rick's portal gun menu; the on/off switch is in Show Me Your Skin's settings

config_fixes.why: Punchy's sword-inspect key (kept in its own file, not options.txt) was on G, the backpack key
Punchy's old sword-inspect key was on J, the portal gun menu key

Punchy!'s first-person animations live in its built-in resource pack, which starts switched off (Punchy shows a 'resource pack disabled' popup). Adds it to the end of the enabled packs if it's missing
REI's 'show recipe' on R also triggered Inventory Profiles Next's sort; recipe moves to Y, next to REI's U for uses
AutoSwitch swapped to flint and steel when right-clicking a creeper, which lights it
Distant Horizons defaults to 256 chunks of far terrain, which maxed out the host laptop's GPU. With C2ME, Lithium, and Sodium, 128 runs smoothly (tested 10/23/2026); 256 is still too far
Moves PCs that still have the pack's old 48-chunk setting up to the new 128. Any other value is a player's own choice and stays
Distant Horizons: 16x fewer far-terrain pieces near the edge of view
Distant Horizons: simpler far-off overhangs and caves
Distant Horizons: no extra full-screen shading pass (shaders shade anyway)
Distant Horizons: no far-off clouds (vanilla clouds are off too)
Distant Horizons: far-off water drawn solid, saving a pass
Distant Horizons: build only the rough surface for far terrain, not full chunks
Distant Horizons used 8 of the laptop's 16 threads at full speed alongside C2ME's world generation, starving the game's own server thread; 4 still builds the far view

config_seed.why: Forge Labs' settings: biome swaps (jungle, badlands, cherry grove, meadow, savanna, snowy plains become pine taiga, fen, shrubland) and Bad Mobs bans (no vanilla hostiles, farm animals, villagers). Copied only where the file is missing
